q.q: A national park ecosystem has living parts and nonliving parts. Which of these is a nonliving part?
An alligator would survive well in a snowy mountain forest.
Wolves came back to Yellowstone in 1995. What happened next?
o: The wolves ate all the plants.
Nothing else in the park changed.
The wolves changed how elk behaved, and that affected plants like willows.
The elk all moved to Florida.

q.q: Maria's park presentation must show a food web and a conservation effort. What do scientists call requirements like these?
Which one is the strongest scientific evidence for a presentation about Yellowstone?
o: Gray wolves hunt in packs, which lets them catch elk much bigger than one wolf could.

q.q: A long dry season hits the Everglades. Which of these living things there could be affected? Choose ALL that are correct.

o: Living things never affect each other.
Living things depend on each other, so a change to one can affect the others.

q.q: Which one is an example of people helping an ecosystem?
o: Draining a marsh to build a parking lot
Cutting down mangroves along the shore
Raising a road onto bridges so water can flow into the Everglades

q.q: Fires burned much of Yellowstone in 1988. What did scientists find growing in the burned forest the next spring?
o: Tiny pine seedlings, from seeds that fell when the heat opened the pine cones
Nothing. The forest could never grow back.

q.q: What is the difference between a guess and a conclusion?
o: A guess uses more evidence than a conclusion.
A conclusion is just your favorite answer.
A conclusion is based on evidence you collected, and a guess is not.
